question: Should OpenClaw adopt `sessions.diagnose` and `openclaw sessions diagnose` as a stable core operator interface, including its public finding-code vocabulary and native-client protocol model?
rationale: The implementation is additive and evidence-backed, but it creates a durable cross-client Gateway and CLI contract rather than repairing an established broken behavior.

options.title: Sponsor the core diagnostic surface
options.body: Accept the read-only RPC and CLI as the supported session-triage interface, then require a clean rebase and final merge-result proof.

options.title: Narrow the public vocabulary
options.body: Keep the diagnosis concept but reduce selectors, findings, or client exposure before establishing the long-term contract.

options.title: Defer the core API
options.body: Pause or close this implementation if maintainers prefer existing status, tail, and logs until a smaller core boundary is designed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core diagnostic surface
recommendation.body: Accept the read-only RPC and CLI as the supported session-triage interface, then require a clean rebase and final merge-result proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Adjacent Gateway session-diagnostics work makes this the strongest available routing signal, though direct ownership history was not available from the failed read-only shell.
